3. The suit jote measuring 0.89 acre of land originally belonged to Bashiruddin, his name duly recorded in the last S.A. khatian. Bashiruddin died leaving behind wife Sahejannessa, five sons Farizuddin, Shamsul Hoque, Abu Taher, Abdul Bari the defendant in suit Md. Shahidul Islam, the plaintiff in suit and three daughters Mehera Khatun, Abeda Khatun and Rasheda Khatun. 

 4. Bashiruddin had other properties which were under amicable possession of the co-sharers. The daughters of Bashuiruddin relinquished their share in favour of their brothers in the suit jote. Sahezannessa by a registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj No. 13022 dated 11.07.1987 gifted her share to the plaintiffs. Five sons equally partitioned the rest land of the suit khatian and accordingly, each son got 0.1550 acre of land. The defendant by a registered sale deed No. 5477 dated 20.04.1991 sold 0.03 acre of land to one Mahmuda Khatun and thereafter by a registered sale deed dated 01.03.1998 bearing No. 2581 sold 0.0925 acre of land to Mosammat Sahera Khatun. The defendant further along with his other brothers and some of their heirs by a registered deed of exchange dated 25.09.1980 bearing No. 26632 transferred 0.17 acre of land to plaintiff and by virtue of the said deed the defendant transferred 0.0425 acre of land to the plaintiff. 

 5. As per amicable family partition three sisters got 0.27 acre of land out of 0.38 acre of Plot No. 2795 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 1100 corresponding S.A. khatian No. 1005 and in the said khatian Abdul Bari got the rest 0.11 acre which he sold to one Matiar Rahman by a registered deed dated 04.09.1980. So far as the land measuring 1.35 acres of Plot No. 2718 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 431/7 corresponding S.A khatian No. 441 is concerned the original owner Bashiruddin during his lifetime by a registered deed of sale dated 14.08.1972 bearing No. 28853 transferred 0.48 acre land and while in possession of the rest 0.87 acre died leaving behind wife Sahezannessa who got 0.1087 acre, five sons got 0.1175 acre each and three daughters got 0.0575 acre each. Three brothers namely Fariz, Shamsul alias Shamsher and Abdul Bari by a registered deed of sale dated 08.03.1979 bearing No. 8066 sold 0.51 acre to the defendant. By virtue of the said deed, the defendant actually got 0.0325 acre of land since the aforesaid three brothers sold excess to their admitted share. The defendant sold 0.72 acre of land, in excess to his admitted share to one Abdul Khaleque Siddique by a registered Sale deed dated 12.07.1980 bearing No. 22025. 

 6. The defendant transferred his entire share in all ejmal khatians and being titless in the paternal properties in the aforementioned manner shifted to Hazarihat with his family and started living there permanently. After a long time he decided to live with close proximity of his paternal property. For the purpose of erecting house and requested the plaintiff to allow him to erect two chala ghar adjacent to plaintiff’s house and accordingly, the plaintiff accorded permission to defendant to erect chala ghar on 0.02 acre of land which is a part of the plaintiff’s residential house, temporarily. After two years the plaintiff when in his need of the said land requested the defendant to vacate and surrender the land, the defendant refused. Lastly, on 15.11.2013, the plaintiff finally demanded vacant possession of the land but the defendant denied to do so, and hence, the plaintiff filed the present suit for recovery of khas possession of 0.02 acre of land demolishing the structure erected thereon.
